#| label: load-libraries

library(ComplexUpset)

```

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
font_add_google("Source Sans 3", "Source Sans 3")
showtext_auto()
# Must match `dpi:` in the YAML header. If they disagree, showtext sizes every glyph
# against the wrong resolution.
showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

LNCRNA_REF_BIOTYPES <- "lncRNA"

base_theme <- theme(
  strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = "black"),
  plot.background = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
  panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 10) + base_theme)

update_geom_defaults("text",  list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 8 / .pt))
update_geom_defaults("label", list(family = "Source Sans 3", size = 8 / .pt))

# --- Shared log axes ---------------------------------------------------------
# Every log-scaled axis in this report goes through these, so tick labels read
# 1,000 rather than a mixture of 1,000 and 1e+03.
#
# expand_top adds headroom above the highest bar. Set it wherever count labels
# are drawn on top of bars, otherwise the topmost label is clipped by the panel
# edge.

scale_y_log10_std <- function(expand_top = FALSE, ...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    expand = if (expand_top) expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)) else waiver(),
    ...
  )
}

scale_x_log10_std <- function(...) {
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = scales::breaks_log(),
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    ...
  )
}

# Exon counts are small integers, so the default log breaks (1, 3, 10, 30) read
# oddly for a number of exons. Force integer breaks instead. The axis stays
# logarithmic because the distribution is heavily skewed towards 1-2 exons.
scale_y_log10_exons <- function(...) {
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
    labels = scales::label_comma(accuracy = 1),
    ...
  )
}

# --- Palette -----------------------------------------------------------------

options(
  ggplot2.discrete.fill = function(...) scale_fill_viridis_d(..., option = "P", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8),
  ggplot2.discrete.colour = function(...) scale_colour_viridis_d(..., option = "P", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8)
)

# --- Chromosome ordering -----------------------------------------------------
# Facet chromosomes in genomic order (1, 2, ... 10, 11 ... X, Y, MT) rather than
# the alphabetical order a plain sort() gives, which would interleave 10 and 11
# between 1 and 2.
#
# The optional chr prefix is stripped before the numeric test. Ensembl names
# contigs "1" while GENCODE names them "chr1"; without stripping, no GENCODE
# name matches the numeric pattern and every chromosome falls through to the
# alphabetical branch.

order_chromosomes <- function(x) {
  values <- unique(as.character(x))
  bare <- sub("^chr", "", values, ignore.case = TRUE)

  is_numeric_chr <- grepl("^[0-9]+$", bare)
  numeric_sorted <- values[is_numeric_chr][order(as.numeric(bare[is_numeric_chr]))]
  other_sorted <- sort(values[!is_numeric_chr])

  # droplevels so a chromosome absent from the data never reserves an empty panel
  droplevels(factor(x, levels = c(numeric_sorted, other_sorted)))
}

# --- Chromosome distribution figures -----------------------------------------
# Ensembl and GENCODE both mix hundreds of unplaced contigs (GL000195.1,
# KI270728.1) in with the real chromosomes. On a GENCODE v50 run, 47 of 72
# seqnames were scaffolds carrying 1-12 transcripts each. Pattern rather than a
# fixed list: the pipeline runs on any Ensembl/GENCODE organism, so this also has
# to cover roman-numeral (yeast I-XVI), arm-suffixed (fly 2L/3R) and organelle
# names.
is_assembled_chromosome <- function(x) {
  bare <- toupper(sub("^chr", "", as.character(x), ignore.case = TRUE))
  grepl("^([0-9]{1,2}[A-Z]?|[IVXL]{1,6}|[XYZW]|M|MT|MITO|MTDNA|PT|PLTD)$", bare)
}

# --- Count lollipops ---------------------------------------------------------
# Counts across two categorical axes: the first spread along x, the second given
# one facet row each, with the exact number printed above every point.
#
# The count axis is a pseudo-log. `scales::pseudo_log_trans` is log-like above 1
# but, unlike log10, is defined at zero, so a category with no transcripts sits on
# the baseline as a hollow point labelled 0. That distinction matters: a category
# genuinely absent from the data and a category that could not be drawn look
# identical otherwise. Missing combinations are completed to zero for the same
# reason rather than dropped.
#
# `df` needs one row per cell with a `count` column.
COUNT_TRANS  <- scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10)
COUNT_BREAKS <- c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1000000)

plot_count_lollipop <- function(df, x, y, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                                x_lab = NULL, count_lab = "Transcripts",
                                facet = NULL, angle_x = 90,
                                complete_grid = TRUE, free_x = FALSE) {

  # complete_grid fills every missing combination with a zero, which is right when
  # the combination could have occurred and did not -- a chromosome carrying none
  # of a biotype is a real measurement.

  full <- if (!complete_grid) {
    df
  } else if (is.null(facet)) {
    tidyr::complete(df, {{ x }}, {{ y }}, fill = list(count = 0))
  } else {
    tidyr::complete(df, {{ x }}, {{ y }}, .data[[facet]], fill = list(count = 0))
  }
  full <- dplyr::mutate(full,
                        .row = as.factor({{ y }}),
                        .col = as.factor({{ x }}))

  p <- ggplot(full, aes(x = .col, y = count)) +
    geom_segment(aes(xend = .col, yend = 0, colour = .row), linewidth = 0.55) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = .row, shape = count > 0), size = 2.4,
               fill = "white", stroke = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = format(count, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
              vjust = -1) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.85, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(trans  = COUNT_TRANS,
                       breaks = COUNT_BREAKS,
                       labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ","),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.25))) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = angle_x,
                                   hjust = if (angle_x == 0) 0.5 else 1,
                                   vjust = if (angle_x == 90) 0.5 else 1),
      plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = x_lab, y = count_lab)

  scl <- if (free_x) "free" else "free_y"
  if (is.null(facet)) {
    p + facet_wrap(vars(.row), ncol = 1, scales = scl, strip.position = "right")
  } else {
    p + facet_grid(rows = vars(.row), cols = vars(.data[[facet]]), scales = scl,
                   space = if (free_x) "free_x" else "fixed")
  }
}

plot_chr_distribution <- function(df, title, subtitle) {
  plot_count_lollipop(df, x = chromosome, y = biotype,
                      title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
                      x_lab = "Chromosome") +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 0),
      plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0)
    )
}

plot_bar_counts <- function(df, x, y, fill = NULL, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                            x_lab = NULL, y_lab = "Count", legend_name = NULL) {
  fill_q <- rlang::enquo(fill)


  show_legend <- !rlang::quo_is_null(fill_q)
  fill_map    <- if (show_legend) fill_q else rlang::enquo(x)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = {{ y }}, fill = !!fill_map)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = format({{ y }}, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
              position = position_dodge2(width = 0.7, preserve = "single"),
              vjust = -0.5) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)),
                       labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "P", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8, name = legend_name) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      legend.position    = if (show_legend) "top" else "none",
      plot.title         = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = x_lab, y = y_lab)
  p
}

# A category with no rows is dropped rather than drawn as an empty panel. Returns
# the named list with every zero-row entry removed.
drop_empty_groups <- function(groups) {
  keep <- vapply(groups, function(g) !is.null(g) && nrow(g) > 0, logical(1))
  groups[keep]
}

# --- UpSet ------------------------------------------------------------------
# ComplexUpset, wrapped so every call site gets the same axis, ordering and
# annotation treatment.
#
# Sets must be attributes an item can hold *simultaneously*. Mutually exclusive
# categories -- biotype, class code, chromosome -- are not sets: every
# non-singleton intersection would be empty by construction and the matrix would
# be dead space. Those belong in `fill_col` instead, which stacks each bar.
#
# `df` needs one row per item, a logical column per entry in `sets`, and
# optionally `fill_col` naming a categorical column.
plot_upset <- function(df, sets, fill_col = NULL, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                       max_intersections = 12) {

  placeholder <- function(msg) {
    ggplot() +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = msg, colour = "grey25") +
      theme_void() +
      labs(title = title) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  }

  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(placeholder("No transcripts to plot."))

  present <- sets[vapply(sets, function(s) s %in% names(df), logical(1))]
  if (!length(present)) {
    return(placeholder(sprintf("None of the expected columns are present: %s.",
                               paste(sets, collapse = ", "))))
  }

  d <- as.data.frame(df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
                         
  for (s in present) d[[s]] <- !is.na(d[[s]]) & as.logical(d[[s]])

  has_fill <- !is.null(fill_col) && fill_col %in% names(d)

  if (has_fill && !is.factor(d[[fill_col]])) d[[fill_col]] <- factor(d[[fill_col]])

  size_layer <- if (has_fill) {
    ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
      counts = TRUE, text = list(vjust = -0.5),
      bar_number_threshold = Inf,
      mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = .data[[fill_col]]))
  } else {
    ComplexUpset::intersection_size(
      counts = TRUE, text = list(vjust = -0.5),
      bar_number_threshold = Inf)
  }

  size_layer <- size_layer +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)),
      labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ","))

  if (has_fill) {
    size_layer <- size_layer +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9, name = NULL)
  }

  p <- ComplexUpset::upset(
    d,
    intersect             = present,
    name                  = "",
    n_intersections       = max_intersections,
    min_degree            = 0,          # keep the "none of these sets" bar
    sort_intersections_by = "cardinality",
    base_annotations      = list(Transcripts = size_layer),
    set_sizes             = ComplexUpset::upset_set_size(position = "right") +
                              ggplot2::geom_text(
                                ggplot2::aes(label = ggplot2::after_stat(count)),
                                stat = "count", hjust = 1.15,
                                colour = "white") +
                              ggplot2::ylab("Set size"),
    # ComplexUpset builds a theme per component rather than inheriting the one set
    # by theme_set(), so the font has to be injected here or the matrix, the set
    # sizes and the intersection bars each fall back to the ggplot default.
    themes                = ComplexUpset::upset_default_themes(
                              text = ggplot2::element_text(family = "Source Sans 3",
                                                           size = 10)),
    width_ratio           = 0.3
  )

  p <- p & ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  if (!is.null(title) || !is.null(subtitle)) {
    p <- p + patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = title, subtitle = subtitle,
      theme = ggplot2::theme(
        plot.title    = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5)))
  }
  p
}
```

## Introduction

This report provides a detailed analysis of a transcriptome assembled from long-read RNA sequencing data. The primary goal is to identify and characterize both known (annotated) and novel protein-coding and lncRNA transcripts. These results are organized into five sections:

1.  **Assembly Statistics:** A high-level view of the assembly results.
2.  **Sample-level Expression Clustering:** How the samples relate to one another, before and after curation.
3.  **Reference Transcriptome:** Biotypes, sequence length and exon structure of the known transcripts detected in your samples.
4.  **Novel Isoforms:** The same for the newly discovered transcripts, plus the evidence tracked for each.
5.  **Genomic Context:** Coverage and transcript models drawn together at selected loci.

This automated report was generated by the `integrativebioinformatics/pulposeq` pipeline.

<details>

<summary>**Metadatasets curation** — how the assembly was curated and filtered</summary>

Downstream to the assembly with **Bambu** [^1], the raw extended annotations and count matrices from `BambuOutput` were curated and subset to generate a final subset of genes and transcripts that are relevant for downstream analyses. The main curation process involved the following steps:

[^1]: Chen, Ying, et al. "Context-aware transcript quantification from long-read RNA-seq data with Bambu." Nature methods 20.8 (2023): 1187-1195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-01908-w

1.  Any gene or transcript with zero counts across all samples was filtered out (the filtered quantification files are in the results folder `bambu_filter/`).
2.  Novel transcript isoforms were compared to the reference annotation by **GffCompare** [^2] and submitted to coding-potential prediction with **CPC2** [^3], or with **RNAmining** [^4] where that predictor was selected. Each was then routed into one of three categories from its class code, its prediction and the biotype of the reference gene it was matched against.
3.  The structure of the isoforms is characterized, and metadata regarding isoform-level structure is retrieved directly from the reference annotation and assembly GTF files with **rtracklayer**[^5].
4.  Count matrices and GTFs are restricted to the curated set, and biotype and classification attributes are attached to the validated annotations.
5.  Bambu's PCA and expression heatmaps are regenerated from the curated transcriptome, so the sample-level view can be read beside the one built from the raw assembly.
6.  Per-base coverage is written per sample as bigWig, and selected loci are drawn over those tracks with **plotgardener**[^6].
7.  Finally, annotations, count matrices and characterization metadata are standardized into comprehensive metadatasets that are easily accessible for downstream analyses, and the overall statistics of the assembly are summarized in the following sections of this report.

[^2]: Pertea, Geo, and Mihaela Pertea. "GFF utilities: GffRead and GffCompare." F1000Research 9 (2020): ISCB-Comm. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.23297.1

[^3]: Kang, Yu-Jian, et al. "CPC2: a fast and accurate coding potential calculator based on sequence intrinsic features." Nucleic Acids Research 45.W1 (2017): W12-W16. https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkx428

[^4]: Ramos, Thaís AR, et al. "RNAmining: A machine learning stand-alone and web server tool for RNA coding potential prediction." F1000Research 10 (2021): 323. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.52350.2

[^5]: Lawrence, Michael, Robert Gentleman, and Vincent Carey. "rtracklayer: an R package for interfacing with genome browsers." Bioinformatics 25.14 (2009): 1841-1842. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btp328

[^6]: Kramer, Nicole E., et al. "Plotgardener: cultivating precise multi-panel figures in R." Bioinformatics 38.7 (2022): 2042-2045. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btac057

Final validated results are organized into the folders `bambu_validated`, `novel_transcripts` and `ref_transcripts` in the output directory. Per-sample coverage tracks are published to `coverage/` as bigWig, and the genomic context figures to `genomic_context/`.

::: callout-note
## Filtering criteria

A novel transcript is carried forward only if it meets **all** of the following:

- **Length ≥ 200 nt** — the consensus lower bound for a long non-coding RNA, applied to every category so the three stay comparable to one another.
- **A declared strand** (`+` or `-`) — models Bambu could not orient are removed.
- **Non-zero counts** in at least one sample.
- **An accepted gffcompare class code** — `u`, `i`, `x`, `j`, `k`, `o`, `y`, `m` or `n`.

Nothing is filtered on structural evidence. Candidates carrying warning signs are reported with those signs attached, in [Tracking Evidence].
:::

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

</details>

<details>

<summary>**gffcompare class codes** — what each code means</summary>

| Code | Description |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| `u` | Unknown or intergenic |
| `i` | Fully contained within a reference intron (sub-classified as: *sense intronic* or *antisense* *intronic)* |
| `x` | Exonic overlap on the opposite strand (*antisense*) |
| `j` | Multi-exon transcript with at least one splice junction matching reference |
| `k` | Containment of reference transcript |
| `o` | Exonic overlap on the same strand |
| `y` | Contains reference within its introns |
| `m` | Retained intron(s), all introns matched or retained |
| `n` | Retained intron(s), not all introns matched or retained |

Class codes are reported exactly as gffcompare assigns them; pulposeq never recomputes or overrides one.

</details>

<details>

<summary>**How novel models are routed** — the three categories and the rules behind them</summary>

Each admitted model is assigned one of **three categories**, and those categories are the grouping used throughout this report.

**`u`, `i` and `x` share no splice structure with a reference.** `u` has no reference at all, `i` lies wholly inside an intron, and `x` overlaps on the opposite strand. The coding prediction stands on its own here, so it decides alone:

| Prediction | Category                     |
|:-----------|:-----------------------------|
| non-coding | **novel lncRNA candidate**   |
| coding     | **predicted protein-coding** |

A sense-intronic or antisense lncRNA sitting inside a protein-coding locus is still an lncRNA, and both Ensembl and GENCODE annotate them that way.

**`j`, `k`, `o`, `y`, `m` and `n` do share structure with a reference transcript.** A non-coding call carries less weight here: an unproductive isoform of a protein-coding gene — a retained intron, an NMD target, a truncated model — is predicted non-coding too, and calling one a novel lncRNA would assert a new non-coding gene at a locus that already has a coding one. So the reference gene's biotype is taken into account:

| Prediction | Reference gene | Category                     |
|:-----------|:---------------|:-----------------------------|
| coding     | any            | **predicted protein-coding** |
| non-coding | lncRNA         | **novel lncRNA candidate**   |
| non-coding | anything else  | **predicted non-coding**     |

**Predicted non-coding** says a model has no coding potential without asserting what it is, which is as much as the evidence supports for a non-coding isoform of a coding gene.

</details>

<details>

<summary>**Sense and antisense intronic transcripts** — why the orientation is reported separately</summary>

Class code `i` — *fully contained within ref intron* — covers both orientations, and they are not the same finding, so the classification qualifies each as **(sense)** or **(antisense)**. The qualifier is pulposeq's addition; gffcompare's own definition says nothing about strand.

A transcript lying inside an intron **on the host gene's own strand** is sequence-identical to part of that host's **unspliced precursor** — the primary transcript, before its introns are removed. Position alone cannot say whether such a model is an independent transcriptional unit or a fragment of the host still being processed.

**On the opposite strand there is no such ambiguity.** The host's precursor runs the other way and cannot produce it.

The ambiguity comes from splicing, not from coding potential, so it applies to any host carrying introns whatever its biotype — lncRNA genes are transcribed by Pol II and spliced exactly as protein-coding genes are, and the hosts here are frequently lncRNA genes. Sense-intronic candidates are kept, never dropped. They are counted as such in [Tracking Evidence], and each of the ones drawn is shown over its whole host intron in [Genomic Context], where coverage continuous with the flanking exons distinguishes a fragment of the precursor from a discrete transcript.

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence
  [Genomic Context]: #genomic-context

</details>

<details>

<summary>**pulposeq follows the current consensus statement for lncRNA classification**</summary>

Transcriptional complexity poses challenges for the accurate classification of lncRNAs, which are often intergenic, intronic, antisense and/or alternatively spliced transcripts from genes of other distinct biotypes (e.g. protein-coding genes, pseudogenes, etc). Relying solely on the parent locus biotype may oversimplify important aspects of the nature and structure of **any RNA molecule**.

pulposeq adresses this conceptual bottleneck when classifying novel isoforms that overlap functionally distinct loci by implementing a dual-layer classification strategy. Novel isoforms transcribed from previously annotated loci are assigned with individual transcript biotypes that were resolved independently based on:

1.  Coding potential predictions;
2.  Structural features identified based on their length, relationship with reference transcripts and their exon-intron structures.

Consequently, a newly discovered isoform lacking coding potential but originating from a known protein-coding locus or any other gene biotype is classified strictly as a novel lncRNA transcript. This standardization process follows the current recommendations of the consensus statement of Mattick and colleagues [^7] for lncRNA classification and naming.

[^7]: Mattick, J.S., Amaral, P.P., Carninci, P. et al. Long non-coding RNAs: definitions, functions, challenges and recommendations. Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 24, 430–447 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41580-022-00566-8

#### Why the report says *candidate*

A transcript labelled a **novel lncRNA candidate** satisfies the filtering criteria above, is predicted non-coding, and either carries a class code that shares no structure with a reference (`u`, `i`, `x`) or shares structure with a reference gene that is itself an lncRNA. That is a well-defined set, and it is the set this report counts.

It is not a set of validated lncRNAs. A coding-potential prediction is evidence about sequence composition, not about whether a transcript is an independent transcriptional unit. Two situations need evidence the prediction cannot supply:

- A **sense-intronic** model cannot be distinguished from a fragment of its host's unspliced precursor by position alone.
- A model **sharing splice structure with a protein-coding gene** may be an unproductive isoform of that gene rather than a new non-coding locus; these are reported as *predicted non-coding* rather than as lncRNA candidates.

The [Tracking Evidence] section reports what other evidence each candidate carries. Nothing is filtered on that basis: a candidate set with the evidence stated per member is a stronger result than an unqualified count.

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

</details>

## Assembly Statistics

This section presents a quantitative isoform-level overview of the transcriptome assembly. Based on the curated subsets from Bambu, we gathered all metadata of genes and transcripts that were detected and quantified. We categorize these into three groups:

- **Total:** All unique features identified.
- **Annotated:** Features that match an existing reference annotation (e.g., Ensembl). These have IDs starting with `ENS`.
- **Novel:** Features newly discovered by Bambu that are not in the reference annotation. These have IDs starting with `Bambu`.

::: callout-warning
Bambu Read Classes (RCs) that are not compatible with any transcript are classified as incompatible and not considered for isoform-level quantification, but all incompatible RCs are still assignable to genes, and Bambu uses them for gene quantification by default. In order to generate a final curated and relevant subset of gene counts, only genes transcribing compatible and effectively quantified isoforms are kept after the validation process.
:::

```{r}
#| label: run-metrics
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

metrics <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$bambu_metrics, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
vsum    <- tryCatch(read.csv(params$validation_summary, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)

get_metric <- function(k) {
  if (is.null(metrics)) return(NA_character_)
  v <- metrics$value[metrics$metric == k]
  if (length(v)) as.character(v[1]) else NA_character_
}

cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
cat("## Run parameters and validation yield\n\n")

ndr <- get_metric("ndr_used")
cat(sprintf("**Novel discovery rate (NDR):** %s%s\n\n",
            ifelse(is.na(ndr), "not recorded", ndr),
            if (identical(get_metric("ndr_requested"), "auto"))
              " — selected automatically by Bambu" else " — set explicitly"))

if (!is.null(vsum)) {
  # Two decimals: 392,130 of 392,201 is 99.98%, and "100.0%" reads as a curation
  # that lost nothing at all.
  vtab <- data.frame(
    Feature            = vsum$feature_type,
    `Curated set`      = format(vsum$curated_set, big.mark = ","),
    `Total quantified` = format(vsum$total_quantified, big.mark = ","),
    `Recovery %`       = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * vsum$recovery),
    check.names        = FALSE
  )
  if (!is.null(vsum$extended_annotations)) {
    vtab$`Extended annotations` <- format(vsum$extended_annotations, big.mark = ",")
  }
  cat(knitr::kable(vtab, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
  cat(paste("\n\n**Total quantified** is the expressed set: features carrying at least",
            "one count in at least one sample, and the denominator recovery is measured",
            "against. **Extended annotation** is every feature Bambu quantified against,",
            "including those no read supports -- those are outside the curation and are",
            "not counted as losses.\n"))
}
cat("\n:::\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: get-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# List bambu outputs to account for assembled and quantified genes/transcripts
bambu_outputs <- c(
  genes = params$counts_genes,
  transcripts = params$counts_transcript,
  fullLength = params$fl_counts_transcript,
  uniquelyMapped = params$u_counts_transcript
)

# Check if files exist
files_exist <- sapply(bambu_outputs, file.exists)
if (!all(files_exist)) {
  missing_files <- bambu_outputs[!files_exist]
  stop("Error: The following files were not found: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

results_list <- list()
bambu_ids    <- list()
for (name in names(bambu_outputs)) {
  current_file <- bambu_outputs[[name]]
  tryCatch({
    data <- read.delim(current_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
    id_column <- as.character(data[[1]])
    bambu_ids[[name]] <- id_column
    total_count <- nrow(data)
    annotated_count <- sum(startsWith(id_column, "ENS"))
    novel_count <- sum(startsWith(id_column, "Bambu"))
    file_result <- data.frame(Bambu = name, Total = total_count, Annotated = annotated_count, Novel = novel_count)
    results_list[[name]] <- file_result
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Warning: Could not process file '", basename(current_file), "' (named '", name, "'). Skipping.\n", sep = "")
    cat("Error message:", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

# Organize results
if (length(results_list) > 0) {
  bambu_df <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  rownames(bambu_df) <- NULL
  bambu_df <- bambu_df %>%
    mutate(FeatureType = if_else(Bambu == "genes", "Gene", "Transcript")) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")
  write.csv(bambu_df, "Bambu_assembly_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed from the provided list.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-to-plot-overall-assembly-stats
#| include: false

if (!exists("bambu_df")) {
  stop("Error: The data frame 'bambu_df' was not found.")
}
bambu_df$Status <- factor(bambu_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
bambu_df$Bambu <- factor(bambu_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("genes", "transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))

detected_tx <- unique(bambu_ids$transcripts)
tx_support  <- data.frame(
  transcript_id         = detected_tx,
  Status                = ifelse(startsWith(detected_tx, "Bambu"), "Novel", "Annotated"),
  `full-length support` = detected_tx %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
  `unique support`      = detected_tx %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped,
  check.names           = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors      = FALSE
)
```

::: callout-tip
## How to read panel B

Bambu writes three transcript count matrices, and the second two are subsets of the first:

- **Total** — every transcript with a non-zero estimated count.
- **Full-length support** — the transcript has reads spanning it end to end, from its start to its termination site.
- **Unique support** — the transcript has reads compatible with it and with no other isoform, so those reads are assigned to it directly rather than shared out.

A transcript can have both, one, or neither, so the three totals overlap and are not plotted side by side. Panel B splits them into the four combinations instead: read a bar by looking down at the dot matrix, where a filled dot means that bar has that kind of support. The bars left of the matrix are the set sizes.

Support says how directly a transcript was measured; nothing is discarded on this basis. A transcript in the *neither* bar was quantified only by expectation-maximisation, so its count is an inference from reads it shares with other isoforms.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-gene-transcript-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Summary of assembled genes and transcripts.** (A) Genes identified by Bambu, split into total, annotated and novel. (B) Every detected transcript, grouped by the kind of read support it has. A transcript can hold both kinds at once, so the bars are not the three nested totals of the count matrices but the four mutually exclusive combinations those totals imply: the dot matrix below each bar reads as *full-length support*, *unique support*, *both* or *neither*, filled dots marking which supports the bar has. The bars to the left of the matrix give each set's overall size. Bars are stacked by annotated vs novel. Nearly every novel model carries both kinds of support -- Bambu calls novel isoforms from full-length read classes -- so the other three bars are almost entirely annotated. The *neither* bar holds transcripts with no full-length and no uniquely-mapping read of their own; they are quantified purely by expectation-maximisation, from reads distributed across the isoforms they are compatible with."

bambu_gene_data <- bambu_df %>% filter(FeatureType == "Gene")

# Genes are a bar chart and transcripts an UpSet, because Bambu writes full-length
# and unique matrices only for transcripts. A gene has no set to belong to, so there
# is nothing to intersect.
gene_bar <- plot_bar_counts(
  bambu_gene_data, x = Status, y = Count,
  title = "Genes", x_lab = NULL, y_lab = "No. of genes")

tx_upset <- plot_upset(
  tx_support,
  sets        = c("full-length support", "unique support"),
  fill_col    = "Status",
  title       = "Transcripts",
  subtitle    = "Read-level support stratification")

plot_grid(gene_bar, tx_upset, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(0.7, 1.3),
          labels = "AUTO", label_y = 0.98)
```

#### RNA biotypes

```{r}
#| label: get-lnc-pc-assembly-stats
#| include: false

# --- 1A. Check if Annotated Transcriptome Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The annotated transcriptome metadata file was not found at: ", params$transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 1B. Check if Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata exists ---
if (!file.exists(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)) {
  stop("Error: The novel transcript metadata file was not found at: ", params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}

# --- 2A. Import Annotated Transcriptome Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  ann_txome <- read.csv(params$transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading annotated transcriptome metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# Collapse the older lncRNA vocabularies onto "lncRNA" once, here, so every
# `gene_biotype == "lncRNA"` downstream is right for an archived annotation as well
# as a current one. Only gene_biotype: transcript_biotype is left as the annotation
# wrote it, since the figures that break lncRNA genes down by transcript biotype are
# there to show exactly that detail.
ann_txome$gene_biotype[ann_txome$gene_biotype %in% LNCRNA_REF_BIOTYPES] <- "lncRNA"

# --- 2B. Import Novel lncRNA/PC Metadata ---
tryCatch({
  novel_tx <- read.csv(params$novel_transcriptome_meta)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Critical Error reading novel transcript metadata file: ", e$message)
})

# The three categories a novel model is routed into. Display labels are defined once
# here and reused throughout the report, so a category is named identically in every
# figure, table and caption.
NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(
  novel_lncRNA         = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  novel_protein_coding = "predicted protein-coding",
  novel_non_coding     = "predicted non-coding"
)

# Read from transcript_biotype, never re-derived from the coding prediction. The
# prediction on its own cannot separate a novel lncRNA candidate from a predicted
# non-coding model -- both are called non-coding, and what distinguishes them is the
# biotype of the reference gene the model shares structure with.
if (!"transcript_biotype" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
  stop("`transcript_biotype` is missing from ", params$novel_transcriptome_meta,
       ". The report cannot assign novel categories without it, and the coding ",
       "prediction is not a substitute.", call. = FALSE)
}

novel_tx$biotype <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS[novel_tx$transcript_biotype])
novel_tx$biotype[is.na(novel_tx$biotype)] <- "novel (unclassified)"

raw_nov_pc_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "predicted protein-coding"])
raw_nov_lnc_tx <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate"])
raw_nov_nc_tx  <- unique(novel_tx$qry_id[novel_tx$biotype == "predicted non-coding"])

# --- 3. Bambu identifiers ---
# `bambu_ids` was populated in get-overall-assembly-stats, from the same read that
# counted the matrices. These files run to hundreds of thousands of rows on a full
# annotation, so they are read once.

# Identify if annotated transcript IDs contain versioning suffix
if (any(grepl("\\.", bambu_ids$transcripts))) {
  version_suffix <- TRUE
} else {
  version_suffix <- FALSE
}

# --- 4. Extract ID vectors for each category (Transcripts Only) ---
ids <- list(
  # Protein-coding
  ann_pc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "protein_coding"])
  },
  
  # lncRNAs
  ann_lnc_tx = if (version_suffix) {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id_version[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  } else {
    unique(ann_txome$ensembl_transcript_id[ann_txome$gene_biotype == "lncRNA"])
  },

  # Filter to only include true novel protein-coding features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_pc_tx = raw_nov_pc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_pc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Filter to only include true novel lncRNA features (starting with "Bambu")
  nov_lnc_tx = raw_nov_lnc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_lnc_tx, "Bambu")],

  # Intron-retention events are a third category, not a subset of either of the
  # above -- omitting them here would drop them from every summary below.
  nov_nc_tx = raw_nov_nc_tx[startsWith(raw_nov_nc_tx, "Bambu")]
)

# Helper function to count overlaps between Bambu outputs and our target IDs
count_overlap <- function(bambu_set, target_ids) {
  if (is.null(bambu_set) || length(bambu_set) == 0) return(0)
  sum(bambu_set %in% target_ids)
}

# --- 5. Quantify across categories ---
results_biotype <- list()

BIOTYPE_LABELS <- c(pc = "Protein-coding", lnc = "lncRNA", nc = "Non-coding")

for (bt in names(BIOTYPE_LABELS)) {
  biotype_label <- unname(BIOTYPE_LABELS[bt])

  # Transcript Level (Check all three transcript files)
  for (tx_cat in c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")) {
    # Intron retention exists only as a novel category -- there is no annotated
    # counterpart to look up, so ann_pc/ann_lnc have no ann_ir sibling.
    ann_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("ann_", bt, "_tx")]])
    nov_t <- count_overlap(bambu_ids[[tx_cat]], ids[[paste0("nov_", bt, "_tx")]])
    tot_t <- ann_t + nov_t
    
    results_biotype[[paste0(bt, "_", tx_cat)]] <- data.frame(
      FeatureType = "Transcript", Biotype = biotype_label, Bambu = tx_cat,
      Total = tot_t, Annotated = ann_t, Novel = nov_t
    )
  }
}

# --- 6. Organize and Save Results ---
if (length(results_biotype) > 0) {
  biotype_df <- do.call(rbind, results_biotype) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(Total, Annotated, Novel), names_to = "Status", values_to = "Count")

  # Ensure proper factor ordering
  biotype_df$Status <- factor(biotype_df$Status, levels = c("Total", "Annotated", "Novel"))
  biotype_df$Bambu <- factor(biotype_df$Bambu, levels = rev(c("transcripts", "fullLength", "uniquelyMapped")))

  write.csv(biotype_df, "Bambu_lncRNA_PC_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("No files were successfully processed to build the biotype summary.\n")
}
```

Bambu reports each transcript in three matrices: all assigned reads, reads spanning the transcript's full structure, and reads mapping to it uniquely. The three are **nested** — full-length and unique support are both subsets of total — so the informative question is not how many transcripts appear in each, but which transcripts appear in *both*.

A transcript with full-length **and** unique support is evidenced directly. One with neither was quantified entirely from expectation-maximisation over reads that never spanned it, and is the weakest thing in the assembly.

```{r}
#| label: support-sets-prep
#| include: false

# One row per detected transcript, with membership of the two support matrices as
# logical columns. Membership, not counts: this figure answers "which transcripts
# have which kinds of evidence", and the count distributions come later.
support_category <- c(
  ann_pc_tx  = "annotated protein-coding",
  ann_lnc_tx = "annotated lncRNA",
  nov_pc_tx  = "predicted protein-coding",
  nov_lnc_tx = "novel lncRNA candidate",
  nov_nc_tx  = "predicted non-coding"
)

detected <- unique(bambu_ids$transcripts)

cat_of <- rep(NA_character_, length(detected))
for (k in names(support_category)) {
  hit <- is.na(cat_of) & detected %in% ids[[k]]
  cat_of[hit] <- support_category[[k]]
}

support_sets <- data.frame(
  transcript_id            = detected,
  category                 = cat_of,
  `full-length support`    = detected %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
  `unique support`         = detected %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped,
  check.names              = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors         = FALSE
)

# Transcripts in the counts matrix that belong to none of the five categories are
# biotypes this figure does not track (small RNAs, pseudogenes and so on). Kept,
# and named, rather than silently dropped.
support_sets$category[is.na(support_sets$category)] <- "other biotypes"
support_sets$category <- factor(
  support_sets$category,
  levels = c("annotated protein-coding", "annotated lncRNA", "other biotypes",
             "predicted protein-coding", "novel lncRNA candidate", "predicted non-coding")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-lnc-pc-stats
#| fig-cap: "**Read support for every transcript in the validated assembly.** Each bar is a distinct combination of evidence, with the dot matrix below showing which kinds of support that combination has. Bars are stacked by transcript category. The *neither* bar — no full-length and no uniquely-mapping read — is quantified purely from expectation-maximisation. The bars to the left of the matrix are the set sizes, one per row, with the count written beside each."

plot_upset(
  support_sets,
  sets      = c("full-length support", "unique support"),
  fill_col  = "category",
  title     = "Read-level support across biotypes",
  subtitle  = ""
)
```

## Sample-level Expression Clustering

Bambu produces a PCA and expression heatmaps summarising how samples relate to one another. The figures below are shown twice: once for the **raw assembly**, exactly as Bambu produced it, and once after the transcriptome has been **validated and curated** by the metadata refinement steps. The raw assembly still contains novel transcript calls that were later discarded, so differences between the two views show how much those discarded calls were influencing the sample-level signal.

```{r}
#| label: plot-availability
#| include: false

plot_params <- list(
  raw_pca                 = params$raw_pca,
  raw_pca_grouped         = params$raw_pca_grouped,
  raw_heatmap_gene        = params$raw_heatmap_gene,
  raw_heatmap_transcript  = params$raw_heatmap_transcript,
  post_pca                = params$post_pca,
  post_pca_grouped        = params$post_pca_grouped,
  post_heatmap_gene       = params$post_heatmap_gene,
  post_heatmap_transcript = params$post_heatmap_transcript
)

# A plot is only embedded if the file is present and non-empty, so a stub run or
# a partially completed execution does not break the render.
plot_available <- vapply(plot_params, function(p) {
  !is.null(p) && file.exists(p) && file.info(p)$size > 0
}, logical(1))

# include_graphics must be handed a vector: called inside a loop it would not be
# auto-printed and nothing would be embedded.
show_plots <- function(keys) {
  paths <- unlist(plot_params[keys][plot_available[keys]], use.names = FALSE)
  if (length(paths) > 0) knitr::include_graphics(paths) else NULL
}
```

## Reference Transcriptome

In this section, we focus exclusively on the **annotated** portion of the transcriptome. These are transcripts that match known entries in public databases. By analyzing their biotypes, lengths, and exon structures, we can understand the composition of the known transcriptome in our samples and establish a baseline for comparison with novel transcripts.

### Biotypes

Biotypes classify RNAs based on their function or characteristics (e.g., `protein_coding`, `lncRNA`, `miRNA`).

```{r}
#| label: data-prep-annotated
#| include: false

# Load and prepare data
summary_data <- ann_txome %>% 
  group_by(gene_biotype, transcript_biotype) %>% 
  summarise(count = n_distinct(ensembl_transcript_id_version), .groups = 'drop')

# Categorize biotypes
protein_coding <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding")
lncRNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype == "lncRNA")
pseudogene_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene")) %>% mutate(category = "Pseudogene")
small_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA"))
Tcell_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("TR_V_gene", "TR_J_gene", "TR_D_gene", "TR_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "TCR elements")
IG_RNAs <- summary_data %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("IG_V_gene", "IG_J_gene", "IG_D_gene", "IG_C_gene")) %>% mutate(category = "Immunoglobulin elements")

# Gather all biotypes that have already been classified above
classified_biotypes <- unique(c(
  protein_coding$gene_biotype,
  lncRNAs$gene_biotype,
  pseudogene_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  small_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  Tcell_RNAs$gene_biotype,
  IG_RNAs$gene_biotype
))

other_RNAs_explicit <- summary_data %>%
  filter(!gene_biotype %in% classified_biotypes) %>%
  mutate(category = "all other biotypes")

biotype_groups <- drop_empty_groups(list(
  `Protein-coding`  = protein_coding,
  `lncRNA`          = lncRNAs,
  `Small RNAs`      = small_RNAs,
  `Pseudogenes`     = pseudogene_RNAs,
  `TCR elements`    = Tcell_RNAs,
  `IG elements`     = IG_RNAs,
  `Other biotypes`  = other_RNAs_explicit
))

create_plot <- function(data, title) {
  d <- data %>%
    dplyr::group_by(transcript_biotype) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.grp = "")

  plot_count_lollipop(d, x = transcript_biotype, y = .grp,
                      title = title,
                      x_lab = "Transcript biotype", count_lab = "Transcripts",
                      angle_x = 90, complete_grid = FALSE) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
      strip.text    = element_blank(),
      plot.title    = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      plot.margin   = margin(0.4, 1, 0.4, 1, "cm")
    )
}

```

#### Transcript biotype diversity

Each tab holds one category group, with that group's transcript biotypes along the x axis and the exact transcript count printed above each point. Counts are summed across the gene biotypes in the group.

Only groups actually present in the supplied annotation get a tab.

```{r}
#| label: fig-biotype-groups
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
#| fig-cap: "Transcript Counts for Major RNA Categories. This panel shows the distribution of transcript biotypes within four main gene biotype categories: Protein-coding RNAs, Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), Small RNAs, and a consolidated group of all other RNA types."

tabs <- lapply(names(biotype_groups), function(nm) {
  knitr::knit_child(
    text = c(
      sprintf("##### %s", nm),
      "",
      "```{r}",
      "#| echo: false",
      sprintf('create_plot(biotype_groups[["%s"]],', nm),
      sprintf('            "%s transcript biotypes")', nm),
      "```",
      ""
    ),
    envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE)
})

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
cat(unlist(tabs), sep = "\n")
cat("\n:::\n\n")
```

#### Gene Biotype Diversity Across Chromosomes

This visualization maps the distribution of different gene biotypes across all chromosomes, revealing genomic hotspots for certain types of genes.

```{r}
#| label: prep-chr-data
#| include: false

chr_gb <- ann_txome %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(str_detect(gene_biotype, "pseudogene"), "pseudogene", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(gene_biotype %in% c("snoRNA", "snRNA", "scaRNA", "sRNA", "rRNA", "misc_RNA", "miRNA"), "small_RNA", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = if_else(!gene_biotype %in% c("pseudogene", "small_RNA", "protein_coding", "lncRNA"), "other", gene_biotype)) %>%
  mutate(chr_class = if_else(is_assembled_chromosome(chromosome_name), "assembled", "scaffold")) %>%
  group_by(chr_class, chromosome = chromosome_name, biotype = gene_biotype) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# droplevels so a biotype absent from the data never reserves an empty panel row
chr_gb$biotype <- droplevels(factor(chr_gb$biotype,
  levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "small_RNA", "pseudogene", "other")))

chr_gb_asm <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "assembled") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = order_chromosomes(chromosome))
chr_gb_scf <- chr_gb %>% filter(chr_class == "scaffold") %>%
  mutate(chromosome = factor(chromosome, levels = sort(unique(chromosome))))

has_scaffolds <- nrow(chr_gb_scf) > 0
```

::: panel-tabset

plot_chr_distribution(

selected_tx <- ann_txome %>% filter(gene_biotype %in% c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
selected_tx$gene_biotype <- factor(selected_tx$gene_biotype, levels = c("protein_coding", "lncRNA", "miRNA", "snoRNA", "snRNA"))
median_stx <- selected_tx %>% group_by(gene_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')
median_pc <- selected_tx %>% filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding") %>% group_by(transcript_biotype) %>% summarise(median_length_txb = median(transcript_length), .groups = 'drop')

## Novel Isoforms

This section characterizes the transcripts that were not present in the reference annotation, across all three routed categories — **novel lncRNA candidates**, models **predicted protein-coding**, and models **predicted non-coding**. Every count below is a count of **candidates**: transcripts that meet the classification criteria and have not yet been shown to be independent transcriptional units. The evidence gathered for them is reported in [Tracking Evidence].

  [Tracking Evidence]: #tracking-evidence

> The metadata behind this section is `novel_transcripts_validated_metadata.csv`, which holds all three categories.

> **About the Tools:**
>
> - **GFFRead:** This tool is used to transform the GTF annotation of the novel transcripts into a FASTA file based on a reference annotation.
> - **GFFCompare:** This tool is used to compare the assembled novel transcripts (from Bambu) against a reference annotation file. It classifies each novel transcript based on its relationship to known transcripts (e.g., a novel isoform of a known gene, a transcript in an intergenic region, etc).
> - **CPC2 / RNAmining:** The selected coding-potential predictor analyses the sequence of each novel transcript to call it protein-coding or non-coding. CPC2 is the default; RNAmining is available as an alternative.

### Biotypes and Classification

```{r}
#| label: load-data-novel
#| include: false

class_counts <- novel_tx %>% group_by(biotype, classification) %>% summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')

# One facet row per routed category.
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-novel-biotypes-and-classes
#| fig-cap: "**GFFCompare classification of the novel candidates.** Counts per classification, one facet row per routed category."

p20 <- plot_count_lollipop(
  class_counts, x = classification, y = biotype,
  title = "GFFCompare classification of novel protein-coding and lncRNA candidates",
  x_lab = "Classification", count_lab = "Transcripts", angle_x = 90
) + theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
p20
```

#### What each novel call was compared against

Every novel model except the intergenic ones (`u`) was matched to a reference transcript. The reference is recorded at both the gene and the transcript level, and where they disagree the transcript level is the one that says what the model actually contains.

```{r}
#| label: prep-ref-biotype
#| include: false

REF_LEVEL_LABELS <- c(ref_gene       = "reference gene biotype",
                      ref_transcript = "reference transcript biotype")

# Intergenic models are excluded: they have no reference, so a "no reference" bar
# spanning the whole category would say nothing about the annotation.
ref_bt_long <- NULL
if (all(c("ref_gene_biotype", "ref_transcript_biotype") %in% names(novel_tx))) {
  tidy_bt <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x)
    x[is.na(x) | !nzchar(x)] <- "no reference"
    x
  }
  ref_bt_long <- novel_tx %>%
    filter(!is.na(class_code), class_code != "u") %>%
    mutate(ref_gene       = tidy_bt(ref_gene_biotype),
           ref_transcript = tidy_bt(ref_transcript_biotype)) %>%
    select(qry_id, class_code, biotype, classification, ref_gene, ref_transcript) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(ref_gene, ref_transcript),
                 names_to = "level", values_to = "ref_biotype") %>%
    mutate(level = unname(REF_LEVEL_LABELS[level]))
}
has_ref_bt <- !is.null(ref_bt_long) && nrow(ref_bt_long) > 0

# Class codes that share splice structure with a reference transcript, and the
# categories that actually have any. Filtering here rather than skipping inside the
# loop keeps the panel count equal to length(related_cats), which is what the
# subfigure lettering counts off.
RELATED_CODES <- c("j", "k", "o", "y", "m", "n")

related_cats <- character(0)
if (has_ref_bt) {
  related_cats <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS)
  related_cats <- related_cats[vapply(related_cats, function(cn)
    any(ref_bt_long$biotype == cn & ref_bt_long$class_code %in% RELATED_CODES),
    logical(1))]
}
has_related <- length(related_cats) > 0
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lnc-ix-ref-biotype
#| fig-cap: "**Reference biotypes behind the intronic and antisense novel lncRNA candidates.** Class codes `i` and `x` become lncRNA candidates on the coding prediction alone, whatever the reference gene is, so this figure says what those references actually were. Columns are the gene and transcript level of the reference; rows are the classification. A combination absent from the data reads as a labelled 0."
#| eval: !expr has_ref_bt

lnc_ix <- ref_bt_long %>%
  filter(biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate", class_code %in% c("i", "x")) %>%
  count(level, classification, ref_biotype, name = "count")

if (nrow(lnc_ix)) {
  plot_count_lollipop(
    lnc_ix, x = ref_biotype, y = classification, facet = "level",
    title = "Novel lncRNA candidates: intronic and antisense",
    subtitle = "",
    x_lab = "Reference biotype", count_lab = "Candidates", angle_x = 90) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5), 
          strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
} else {
  cat("No intronic or antisense novel lncRNA candidates in this run.\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-related-ref-biotype
#| fig-cap: "**Reference biotypes behind the remaining novel calls.** These class codes share splice structure with a reference transcript, so the reference gene's biotype is part of how they are routed. Columns are the gene and transcript level of the reference, rows the classification."
#| eval: !expr has_related
#| fig-subcap: true

# One panel per routed category. fig-subcap collects them into a single figure
# lettered (a), (b), (c); without it Quarto repeats the whole caption under every
# panel. It takes `true` or a literal list only -- Quarto validates cell metadata
# against its schema before knitr runs, so `!expr` is rejected there even though
# fig-width, fig-height and eval accept it. The panel title carries the category
# name instead, which the letters cannot.
related <- ref_bt_long %>%
  filter(class_code %in% RELATED_CODES)

for (cat_name in related_cats) {
  d <- related %>%
    filter(biotype == cat_name) %>%
    count(level, classification, ref_biotype, name = "count")

  print(
    plot_count_lollipop(
      d, x = ref_biotype, y = classification, facet = "level",
      title = cat_name,
      x_lab = "Reference biotype", count_lab = "Transcripts", angle_x = 90) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
            strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
  )
}
```

#### Bambu Transcript Classification

A class code says how a novel model sits relative to the reference it was matched against. Bambu's own `txClassDescription` says something the class code cannot: **which part of the model was not already in the annotation** — a new first exon, a new junction, a whole new gene. A `j` model whose only novelty is `newLastExon` and a `j` model that is `allNew` carry the same class code and are not the same claim.

A model can carry several at once — `newFirstJunction:newJunction:newFirstExon` — so they are sets, not categories.

```{r}
#| label: bambu-class-prep
#| include: false

# One row per (transcript, class). Split on the colon rather than matching
# substrings: "newJunction" is a substring of "newLastJunction", so grepl would
# count every newLastJunction model twice.
bambu_class_sets <- NULL
BAMBU_CLASSES    <- character(0)

if ("BambuTxClass" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
  has_class <- !is.na(novel_tx$BambuTxClass) & nzchar(novel_tx$BambuTxClass)

  if (any(has_class)) {
    bc <- novel_tx[has_class, , drop = FALSE]
    class_list    <- strsplit(as.character(bc$BambuTxClass), ":", fixed = TRUE)
    BAMBU_CLASSES <- sort(unique(trimws(unlist(class_list))))

    for (cl in BAMBU_CLASSES) {
      bc[[cl]] <- vapply(class_list, function(x) cl %in% trimws(x), logical(1))
    }
    bc$novel_category <- droplevels(factor(bc$biotype))
    bambu_class_sets  <- bc
  }
}

# An UpSet over one set is a single bar. Below two, the lollipop and the table
# carry the section on their own.
has_bambu_class <- !is.null(bambu_class_sets) && length(BAMBU_CLASSES) >= 2

# --- Bambu class crossed with the gffcompare classification -------------------
# Long form, so a model carrying two classes is counted under both. That makes the
# column totals exceed the number of models, which is what a set membership means
# and is stated in the caption.
bambu_class_cross      <- NULL
has_bambu_class_cross  <- FALSE

bambu_class_table     <- NULL
has_bambu_class_table <- FALSE

if (!is.null(bambu_class_sets)) {
  bambu_long <- bambu_class_sets %>%
    select(qry_id, classification, novel_category, any_of("BambuNDR"),
           all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES),
                 names_to = "bambu_class", values_to = "carries") %>%
    filter(carries)

  if (nrow(bambu_long)) {
    bambu_class_cross <- bambu_long %>%
      count(novel_category, classification, bambu_class, name = "count")
    has_bambu_class_cross <- TRUE

    # NDR is Bambu's per-model score, so a median over a class says how confidently
    # that whole kind of model was called.
    bambu_class_table <- bambu_long %>%
      group_by(`Bambu class` = bambu_class) %>%
      summarise(
        Models = dplyr::n(),
        `Median NDR` = if (!"BambuNDR" %in% names(bambu_long) ||
                           all(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BambuNDR))))) {
          NA_character_
        } else {
          sprintf("%.3f", median(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(BambuNDR)), na.rm = TRUE))
        },
        .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(dplyr::desc(Models))
    has_bambu_class_table <- nrow(bambu_class_table) > 0
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-upset
#| fig-cap: "**Which parts of each novel model were new to the annotation.** Each bar is one exact combination of Bambu transcript classes; the dot matrix below names it. Bars are stacked by the category the model was routed into, and set sizes on the right give how many models carry each class in total. A model with several filled dots needed more than one novel feature to be built."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class

plot_upset(
  bambu_class_sets,
  sets     = BAMBU_CLASSES,
  fill_col = "novel_category",
  title    = "Bambu transcript classes",
  subtitle = sprintf("%s novel models carrying a class",
                     format(nrow(bambu_class_sets), big.mark = ",")))
```

```{r}
#| label: bambu-class-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(bambu_class_sets)) {
  cat("No novel model carries a Bambu transcript class in this run. ",
      "`BambuTxClass` is read from the assembly's `SummarizedExperiment`; ",
      "an empty column means that object did not reach this step.\n")
} else if (!has_bambu_class) {
  cat(sprintf("Every novel model in this run is **%s**, so there are no combinations to plot.\n",
              BAMBU_CLASSES[1]))
}
```

The two vocabularies are not redundant, and where they disagree is where the interesting models are. The figure below crosses them.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-vs-code

A model appears once per class it carries, so a row total can exceed the number of models. A combination absent from the data reads as a labelled 0."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class_cross

plot_count_lollipop(
  bambu_class_cross, x = bambu_class, y = classification, facet = "novel_category",
  x_lab = "Bambu transcript class", count_lab = "Transcripts", angle_x = 90) +

```{r}
#| label: bambu-class-support-prep
#| include: false

# Read support per Bambu class. Long form: a model carrying two classes is counted
# under both, which is the only honest way to describe a set membership.
bambu_class_support <- NULL

if (!is.null(bambu_class_sets) && exists("bambu_ids")) {
  fl_ids <- if (!is.null(bambu_ids$fullLength)) bambu_ids$fullLength else character(0)
  uq_ids <- if (!is.null(bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped)) bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped else character(0)

  bambu_class_support <- bambu_class_sets %>%
    select(qry_id, novel_category, all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = all_of(BAMBU_CLASSES),
                 names_to = "bambu_class", values_to = "carries") %>%
    filter(carries) %>%
    mutate(`full-length support` = qry_id %in% fl_ids,
           `unique support`      = qry_id %in% uq_ids) %>%
    group_by(bambu_class) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
              `full-length` = mean(`full-length support`),
              `unique`      = mean(`unique support`),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(`full-length`, `unique`),
                 names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction")

  if (!nrow(bambu_class_support)) bambu_class_support <- NULL
}

has_bambu_class_support <- !is.null(bambu_class_support)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bambu-class-support
#| fig-cap: "**Read support by Bambu transcript class.** The fraction of models in each class that appear in Bambu's full-length and unique count matrices. A class whose models are rarely spanned end to end was built from reads that did not cover it, whatever its class code says."
#| eval: !expr has_bambu_class_support

ggplot(bambu_class_support,
       aes(x = reorder(bambu_class, -n), y = fraction, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * fraction)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.08), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Read support by Bambu transcript class",
       subtitle = "Fraction of models in each class carrying each kind of support",
       x = NULL, y = "Models with this support", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

#| tbl-cap: "Novel models per Bambu transcript class, with the median NDR Bambu assigned them."

bambu_class_table %>%

#### Read support behind the lncRNA candidates

Full-length and unique support are both subsets of total, so a candidate holds both, one, or neither. The combination worth finding is **neither**: those candidates were quantified entirely from expectation-maximisation over reads that never spanned them and were never unambiguous.

```{r}
#| label: fig-lnc-matrix-support
#| fig-cap: "**Read support for novel lncRNA candidates, by classification.** Each bar is one combination of read support, stacked by classification. Full-length support means reads spanning the whole model; unique support means reads not compatible with any other transcript. A bar with both dots grey would hold candidates quantified purely from expectation-maximisation. Set sizes on the right are the totals per kind of support."

lnc_sets <- novel_tx %>%
  filter(biotype == "novel lncRNA candidate") %>%
  transmute(classification    = factor(classification),
            `full-length support` = qry_id %in% bambu_ids$fullLength,
            `unique support`      = qry_id %in% bambu_ids$uniquelyMapped)

plot_upset(
  lnc_sets,
  sets              = c("full-length support", "unique support"),
  fill_col          = "classification",
  title             = "Read support for novel lncRNA candidates",
  subtitle          = "",
  max_intersections = as.integer(nrow(lnc_sets)))
```
